channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal burning causes deforestation
item.description: Charcoal production is destroying economic trees and contributing to greenhouse gas emissions in Sierra Leone.

item.title: Sierra Leone vice presidents fail to reach presidency
item.description: No vice president has ever been elected president in Sierra Leone, raising questions about the office's succession pathway.

item.title: Female artisanal miners report sexual violence in Kono district
item.description: Women working in abandoned diamond and gold pits in Jaiama Nimikor describe a pattern of rape and harassment while seeking to earn a living.

item.title: sierra leone finance minister defends economic management
item.description: A civil society group called for the finance minister's dismissal, citing economic hardship and debt.

item.title: Mauritius sergeant kept in detention over shooting
item.description: Sergeant Gautam Singh Taukoor faces charges of intimidation and involuntary wounds after a shooting incident on October 9.

item.title: Air Mauritius launches 10-point plan for recovery
item.description: The airline aims to improve operations, customer experience, and costs with a new strategic roadmap.

item.title: Liberia watchdog blasts official benefits
item.description: CENTAL director says US$9,000 salary and US$15,000 housing allowance for CBL deputy governor are excessive.

item.title: Tanzania warns of El Niño rains
item.description: The Tanzania Meteorological Authority forecasts normal to above-normal rainfall from October to January.

item.title: Kenya could be declared Ebola-free in 42 days
item.description: Health CS Aden Duale said Kenya will be declared Ebola-free after 42 days without new cases, following WHO protocols.

item.title: Tshisekedi orders audit of state computer systems
item.description: DR Congo president seeks to identify security flaws and protect sensitive state data amid rising cyber threats.

item.title: Mozambique reopens Palma fuel station by December
item.description: FUNAE expects to restore fuel supply capacity in Palma district by year-end.

item.title: Tanzania urges neighbours to act on Lake Tanganyika pollution
item.description: Permanent Secretary Dr Richard Muyungi called for concrete action beyond policy to save the lake's biodiversity and 13 million people.

item.title: DR Congo's Banana SEZ gets expert approval
item.description: The project in Muanda, Kongo Central, secured a favorable opinion with over $100 million investment planned.

item.title: Liberia's Supreme Court to hear appeal on ousted health chief
item.description: The government is appealing a ruling that ordered reinstatement or compensation for Dr. Dougbeh Christopher Nyan.

item.title: Liberia Supreme Court hears SRIMEX-LPRC fuel pricing dispute
item.description: The court will decide if an arbitration clause in a petroleum storage agreement overrides government fuel price changes.

item.title: Ghana seeks BRICS funding for energy sector
item.description: The nation needs US$4.4 billion for energy investments between 2025 and 2030, with the New Development Bank as a potential source.

item.title: Liberia's House accuses Senate of delaying bills
item.description: Representatives claim some Senate-passed bills have been pending for two years, causing frustration.

item.title: 10 killed in Tonj North communal violence
item.description: Attackers from Akop Payam killed eight residents of Mading Juer Boma and two of their own in Friday night fighting.

item.title: Tanzania avocado exports surpass 2030 target
item.description: Tanzania exported 52,000 tonnes of avocados in the 2025/2026 season, exceeding its 2030 goal.

item.title: Galamsey threatens Ghana gas pipelines
item.description: Illegal miners are digging near Ghana Gas infrastructure, risking energy supply disruptions.

item.title: South Africa cuts fuel levy by up to R3 per litre
item.description: Motorists will see temporary relief from November 4, with further reductions planned until January 5.

item.title: Tanzania Sisal Board partners for women's employment
item.description: The Tanzania Sisal Board and Mwanamke Initiative Foundation will collaborate to train women and youth in sisal product manufacturing.

item.title: Regina Melanie literary prize honours students
item.description: Lenstiti Kreol and the Ministry of Tourism and Culture celebrated young writers at the 6th Regina Melanie Literary Prize.

item.title: Burundi court receives accounts from only 12 of 303 entities
item.description: The Court of Audit president reported that most public entities failed to submit their 2025-2026 financial accounts.

item.title: Chad official promotes peace after farmer-herder clash
item.description: Ahmat Choua Rozi met with community representatives in Salamat to foster reconciliation and prevent future conflict.

item.title: Seychelles prepares for December rainy season
item.description: Government announces measures to mitigate flooding and reduce impact of heavy rains.

item.title: Former Alego Usonga MP Otieno Mak’Onyango dies
item.description: Mak’Onyango, who was detained after the 1982 coup attempt, died in a Nairobi hospital on Sunday.

item.title: Nigerian govt disburses N38.93 billion to 166 institutions
item.description: The Federal Government released funds to improve infrastructure and teaching facilities at universities, polytechnics, and colleges of education.

item.title: Dorcas Society gives UTH 110 wheelchairs
item.description: The donation will improve patient mobility and strengthen health care service delivery at the Lusaka hospital.

item.title: Burundi investor launches solar car charging station
item.description: Electric vehicles offer Burundi economic and environmental benefits by reducing fuel imports and emissions.

item.title: UN condemns murder of Ebola nurse in Bafwasende
item.description: The UN Ebola response office called for an investigation into the killing of a nurse on October 24.

item.title: two trucks overturn in Lagos, kill mother and child
item.description: Two container trucks overturned on a Lagos road, resulting in the tragic deaths of a mother and her child.

item.title: Julius Nainoo elected NDC Berekum West chairman
item.description: Delegates elected Julius Nainoo with 334 votes, unseating incumbent James Ntim who received 302 votes.

item.title: Madagascar updates national health security plan
item.description: The revised National Action Plan for Health Security aims to strengthen the country's response to health emergencies.

item.title: Madagascar police celebrate 65 years of service
item.description: The national police force marked its 65th anniversary with public outreach and recruitment drives.

item.title: Judiciary to rule on deadly clashes at Akol Koor's residence
item.description: A South Sudanese court will deliver a judgment on Monday regarding a lawsuit filed by victims of a November 2024 gunfight.

item.title: South Sudan standards body commends Juba arrests over expired flour
item.description: Eight employees of H Brothers General Trading and Investment Company Limited were detained for allegedly repackaging expired maize flour.

item.title: Fulani groups demand 30% agric budget for livestock
item.description: Pastoralist associations want the livestock ministry funded and 417 grazing reserves gazetted to end farmer-herder conflict.

item.title: foot-and-mouth disease threatens N$2.4 billion livestock value
item.description: Namibia Agricultural Union estimates daily losses of N$13 million due to ongoing marketing disruptions.

item.title: Uganda urges predictable funding for African peace operations
item.description: Kampala calls for joint AU-UN frameworks and structured financial partnerships to ensure long-term stability across the continent.

item.title: FNB Namibia bondholders face November deadline
item.description: Physical bond certificates must be converted to electronic records by November 9 to remain tradable.

item.title: Kojo Kwarteng becomes a lawyer
item.description: Emmanuel Kojo Kwarteng added law to a career in journalism, marketing, and banking.

item.title: Nigeria identifies 53 Ebola contacts, offers weekly support
item.description: The federal government will provide N100,000 weekly to individuals in isolation as it tracks 53 contacts of the confirmed Ebola case.

item.title: Ghanaian education fund supports 61 students with GH¢138,536
item.description: The Upper West Regional Chief Imam Educational Endowment Fund disbursed funds for the 2026/27 academic year, increasing beneficiaries by 38.64%.

item.title: Mozambique boosts investment budget by 3.6 billion meticais
item.description: Government plans to restore flood-damaged infrastructure and public services using LNG revenues.

item.title: Chapo meets Putin at Russia-Africa Summit
item.description: Mozambican President Daniel Chapo will attend the 3rd Russia-Africa Summit and meet with Vladimir Putin.

item.title: Mozambique safari operator wins conservation award
item.description: Zambeze Delta Safaris received recognition at COP17 for combining trophy hunting with wildlife restoration and community development.

item.title: Madagascar U15 team wins three matches in Baku
item.description: The Barea secured victories against Mozambique, New Zealand, and Puerto Rico in the FIFA U15 World Cup.

item.title: Madagascar police numbers increase
item.description: The Ministry of Public Security aims to reduce the ratio of one police officer to 3,000 inhabitants.

item.title: Madagascar U23 team wins fifth friendly match
item.description: The national U23 team, the Barea, defeated Bongolava 8-0 in their sixth preparation match for the U23 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers.

item.title: four arrested in foiled Limpopo ATM bombing plot
item.description: Police seized an AK-47 rifle, 36 rounds of ammunition, and four cellphones from suspects in the Vaalbank area.

item.title: Eswatini MPs seek easier travel with Lesotho, Botswana
item.description: Eswatini parliamentarians met in Lesotho to discuss removing travel barriers with neighbouring countries.

item.title: Eswatini votes on Africa Cup of Nations schedule
item.description: The Confederation of African Football is consulting its 54 member associations on tournament frequency.

item.title: DHL, EIPA train Eswatini MSMEs for export
item.description: A new partnership aims to equip local businesses with skills for international markets and customs.

item.title: Vusi Nova applauds Eswatini musician Young Zesh
item.description: South African artist Vusi Nova praised Young Zesh's song 'KaKhoza' at the Malkerns Country Club Kota Festival.

item.title: 34 Eswatini police graduate with police science diplomas
item.description: The officers gained skills to tackle emerging crimes like cybercrime through a UNESWA and police academy partnership.

item.title: Nigeria plans 30% value-addition for industrial growth
item.description: The RMRDC Director-General stated the plan aims to boost local manufacturing and resource utilization.

item.title: Senegalese footballers score in European leagues
item.description: Nicolas Jackson, Boulaye Dia, and five other players found the net in weekend matches.

item.title: FIFA representative arrives for Guinean football election
item.description: Fatou Camara will monitor the election of the new president and executive committee of the Guinean Football Federation.

item.title: Senegal U20 team eliminated from UFOA-A tournament
item.description: The Lionceaux lost 3-2 to Guinea in the semi-finals, failing to qualify for the Africa Cup of Nations.

item.title: three die in N'Djamena road accident
item.description: A vehicle overturned near Milezi forest after swerving to avoid a motorcycle.

item.title: Senegal minister visits Bissau to discuss election date
item.description: Cheikh Niang arrived Sunday to assess Guinea-Bissau's political situation and a potential new date for general elections.

item.title: Johannesburg runners raise cancer funds
item.description: Thousands of men and boys wore purple Speedos for the 5km Hollard Daredevil Run charity event.

item.title: Mbappé double gives Real Madrid victory over Barcelona
item.description: Kylian Mbappé scored twice to secure a 2-1 win for Real Madrid against FC Barcelona in La Liga on Sunday.

item.title: Le Faso Digital attracts 201 digital innovation entries
item.description: The virtual fair in Ouagadougou concluded with plans for a 2028 international conference on West African online media.

item.title: Burkina Faso minister unveils Sankara statue in Rome
item.description: A two-meter steel sculpture of Thomas Sankara was inaugurated in a park named after him in Rome, Italy.

item.title: Burkina Faso police seize nearly 400 motorbikes in three hours
item.description: Ouagadougou police confiscated motorbikes during a night operation targeting mandatory helmet use.

item.title: Burkina Faso launches sovereignty football league in 2027
item.description: The new competition aims to professionalize football and create 740 direct jobs across the country.

item.title: RSF invasion of El Fasher causes mass displacement and famine risk
item.description: Over 1.19 million people fled into Chad, with 107,000 displaced in initial weeks, facing severe hunger.

item.title: Egypt rejects Nile water security compromise
item.description: President Al-Sisi stated Egypt will not accept a fait accompli regarding its water security from the Nile.

item.title: Socfin worker dies after falling from moving truck
item.description: Sebatu Sengeh, an agriculture carrier, died Friday after attempting to board a utility truck that was in motion.

item.title: Libya reviews rail projects with Russia and China
item.description: Transportation Ministry discusses resuming operations and a potential monorail for Tripoli.

item.title: Signet and De Beers deepen Botswana diamond ties
item.description: The two companies are strengthening their partnership across mining, manufacturing, and retail to boost natural diamond sales.

item.title: Egypt launches patient safety strategy for 2026-2030
item.description: The plan aims to reduce medical errors and improve healthcare standards across all levels of care.

item.title: Benin and UAE sign economic partnership accord
item.description: The agreement aims to reduce tariffs and facilitate market access for services and investors.

item.title: Mnangagwa faces court challenge over term limits
item.description: Zimbabwe's Constitutional Court will hear three challenges in November to President Mnangagwa's bid to serve beyond two terms.

item.title: Mali distributes 200 food kits to vulnerable people
item.description: The kits, part of the 31st Solidarity Month, contain rice, maize, and oil for those in need.

item.title: Franklin Templeton funds hold CFAF 2 billion in Cameroon bonds
item.description: Two investment funds reported CFAF 2.04 billion in Cameroon sovereign bonds with a 5.95% coupon maturing in 2032.

item.title: Lesotho probes oil firms for alleged fraud
item.description: Companies accused of claiming fees for fuel never offloaded at Maseru depot, government to launch audit.

item.title: two men sentenced for 2024 border murder
item.description: Basotho nationals received life sentences in South Africa for a double murder at Maseru Bridge.

item.title: football fans assault officials over juju fears
item.description: Chitipa United supporters invaded a tunnel and attacked Masters FC officials believing juju prevented their team from scoring.

item.title: Lesotho government launches Tebellong bridge project
item.description: Unik Construction will build the Senqu River bridge, expected to improve safety and tourism in Qacha’s Nek.

item.title: Mafeteng Hospital sued M2 million for alleged negligence
item.description: A patient claims he received no medical attention for seven days after a stomach operation in December 2024.

item.title: Global Fund ends Botswana HIV and TB funding by 2030
item.description: Botswana must finance its HIV and tuberculosis programmes entirely from domestic resources after the Global Fund's final grant cycle.

item.title: Botswana investors access Dangote IPO via BDRs
item.description: Access Bank Botswana issues BDRs for Dangote Refinery IPO, opening African market access on the BSE.

item.title: Morocco plans to double e-cigarette tax in 2027
item.description: New tax measures will also apply to refillable devices and components, expanding the definition of e-cigarettes.

item.title: Himra wins 30 million FCFA at Primud awards
item.description: The Ivorian rapper received five trophies including best rap francophone at the October 11, 2025 ceremony in Abidjan.

item.title: Rwanda asks churches to help families
item.description: Prime Minister Nsengiyumva urged religious leaders to strengthen marriage preparation and support household finances.

item.title: Congo assembly president seeks constitutional change for president
item.description: Isidore Mvouba stated Denis Sassou Nguesso is the man for today, tomorrow, and beyond 2031.

item.title: Botswana fails global tax transparency test
item.description: The OECD's 2026 peer review found Botswana lacks required tax information exchange arrangements for multinationals.

item.title: Haiti force receives human remains after soldier disappearance
item.description: The Gang Suppression Force (GSF) received human remains suspected to be those of four missing Salvadoran soldiers.

item.title: Botswana receives one billion Pula diamond dividend
item.description: The newly established Diamond for Development Fund received a one billion Pula transfer from De Beers.

item.title: Morocco U-17 women's team to play World Cup knockout match October 28 or 29
item.description: The Atlas Lionesses will compete in the round of 16 at the Mohammed VI Football Complex near Rabat.

item.title: Chad women learn breast cancer prevention in Abéché
item.description: The Association of Midwives for Sexual and Reproductive Health raised awareness about early detection and dangers.

item.title: HRDC questions police over journalists' assault
item.description: The Human Rights Defenders Coalition demands an investigation into officers who allegedly failed to intervene during an attack on two journalists.

item.title: Club Africain leads TP Mazembe 1-0 at half-time
item.description: Taddaeus Fomakwang scored in added time for Club Africain in their African Champions League qualifier.

item.title: Somalia ex-spy chief hints at Al-Shabaab alliance
item.description: Former intelligence chief Abdullahi Mohamed Ali Sanbalolshe did not rule out cooperation with Al-Shabaab to destabilize the government.

item.title: Senegal PM defends 2050 vision amid budget constraints
item.description: Prime Minister Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed Lô stated that the method for achieving Senegal's 2050 goals will adapt, not the ambition.

item.title: Cape Verde minister attends biodiversity conference
item.description: The minister will join global leaders to accelerate the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework implementation.

item.title: Cape Town shooting leaves five dead
item.description: Eight people were shot in a gang-related incident near Steenberg and Lavender Hill on the Cape Flats.
